title: Mitek Systems – A Buy Based On DCF And Fundamental Analysis
text:
Mitek Systems – A Buy Based On DCF And Fundamental Analysis
I’ve been working on a DCF model on Mitek Systems, Inc. (MITK) for the past couple of weeks. This has included a fairly deep-dive into their SEC filings and financial reports, press releases, news items, and past earnings calls. They announce FY18Q1 earnings this coming Thursday 1/25, but I wanted to put out my analysis prior to the call to give investors some additional information to act on. I’ll be updating my analysis following their first-quarter results and will be following this company closely moving forward.
Introduction to Mitek Systems
I discovered Mitek while scanning through micro/small-cap tech companies that could have growth drivers related to new technologies and adapting markets. Specifically, I was looking for firms with potential exposure to blockchain technology with the stipulation that the underlying company was decent with longevity (I’m looking at you, Long Island Iced Tea I mean Long Blockchain Corp.). Truthfully, I wanted to get out ahead of the market’s reaction to any “blockchain” or “crypto” buzzwords while still holding a solid underlying. I found Mitek to fit this description nicely.
Mitek Systems is a San Diego based software company that develops, markets, and sells mobile capture and identity verification software solutions to businesses. Their technology allows users to remotely deposit checks, open accounts, get insurance quotes, pay bills, and verify their identity by taking pictures of various documents with their smartphones or tablets.
Its mobile technology solutions are provided in two parts: a software development kit (SDK) for mobile capture, and a software platform for image correction, detection, extraction and authentication. They currently serve 6,000 financial service organizations and leading brands across the world. These include names such as PayPal (PYPL), CVS (CVS), Morgan Stanley (MS), Sprint (S), American Express (AXP), Credit Karma and many more.
Mitek’s products are embedded in native mobile apps and mobile optimized websites to facilitate better mobile user experiences and compliant transactions. Their identity verification solutions are for use with digital/mobile onboarding, trust establishment, and to facilitate money movement. Today, the financial services verticals (banks, credit unions, lenders, payments processors, card issuers, insurers, etc.) are their major customers, but they are seeing solid growth in telecommunications, healthcare, travel, retail, sharing economy, and online marketplaces.
Product Lines
1) Mobile Verify is an identity verification solution that can be integrated into mobile apps, mobile websites, and desktop applications. It utilizes artificial intelligence and machine learning to perform algorithmic-based tests that verify the authenticity of thousands of identification document types globally, including passports, driver licenses, and identity cards.
2) Mobile Fill enables the camera to serve as a keyboard allowing consumers to prefill forms with personal data by simply taking a picture of their driver’s license, passport, credit card, or other document. Organizations use Mobile Fill for a variety of purposes, including streamlining the process of opening a checking, savings, or credit card account, paying a bill, etc.
3) Mobile Docs is a mobile document scanning solution. It enables consumers to take photos of documents resulting in scanner-quality images and is used to submit the trailing documents required for digital account opening, lending, and providing supporting documentation.
4) Mobile Deposit allows individuals and businesses to remotely deposit checks using their camera-equipped smartphone or tablet. Currently, 99 of the biggest 100 domestic banks are using this product which is no surprise since it costs a bank 1/10th as much as processing a paper check.
5) Commercial Mobile Deposit Capture uses the same technology as Mobile Deposit, but is specific to small and medium-sized businesses. It adds capabilities such as mobile multi-check capture to help businesses reduce or eliminate their need for check scanners and trips to the ATM or bank branch.
6) Mitek MiSnap is a touch-free automated capture technology which is incorporated across Mitek product lines. A photo is automatically taken when the user positions their device over an item which greatly improves ease of use.
Mitek Systems Fundamentals
Summary Financials and M&A Activity
Mitek has a strong Balance Sheet – they continue to grow their cash balance and working capital on a y/y basis without taking on debt.
(Source: self-made from Mitek SEC filings.)
I expect to see continued M&A activities following their ICAR acquisition in October 2017 and IDChecker acquisition in June 2015. Their primary M&A goal is to employ their cash stash and cash flows from operations to enter new regions and markets with a growing product portfolio. For example, their ICAR acquisition has given Mitek exposure to the Spanish and Latin American markets while enhancing desktop capture capabilities. Additionally, it has broadened Mitek’s network to include ICARs channel distribution partners such as Accenture (ACN). Mitek management sees the ICAR acquisition becoming accretive within FY18.
Company Management
Mitek boasts a strong management team which has positioned the company for strong sustainable growth while capturing shifts in market trends. Jim DeBello, President and CEO since 2003, has an MBA from Harvard University and previously led Qualcomm’s Internet Service division. In his time with Mitek, he has created and implemented the company’s successful strategy to enter the emerging mobile capture and ID verification markets which has generated significant shareholder value. A quick scan of the remaining management roster shows an incredibly strong lineup of leaders coming from companies including Apple, Qualcomm, IBM, Microsoft, and many more.
Investment Thesis
Mitek has transformed into a high growth company (+30% revenue recurring y/y) while reaching profitability in 2015.
(Source: Mitek Q4 2017 Investor Presentation)
They are well positioned to continue growing, led by secular trends driving adoption across their product portfolio. I think that these trends can be wrapped up into two primary categories: (1) digital and mobile transformation and (2) improved security measures arising from recent data breaches and increasing regulations.
(Source: Mitek Q4 2017 Investor Presentation)
Digital and Mobile Transformation
The digital and mobile transformation covers a broad range of industries and technologies. In respect to Mitek, the key market to focus on is financial services (banks, credit unions, lenders, payments processors, card issuers, insurers), but we should also consider telecommunications, healthcare, travel, retail, sharing economy, and other online marketplaces/e-commerce.
(Source: Mitek Q4 2017 Investor Presentation)
The Consumer Identity & Access Management Market (CIAM) is currently pegged at around $10.7 billion and is expected to reach $17 billion by 2020. This market is massive and will cover most every consumer-facing service industry. Mitek is positioned to sell to these companies and institutions with a time/cost saving value proposition along with additional security.
(Source: Javelin Strategy & Research, 2017 Digital Lending Fraud Study)
There is a stark trend towards mobile and electronic banking in lieu of traditional brick and mortar branches. For instance, major banks such as Wells Fargo (WFC), JPMorgan Chase (JPM), and Bank of America (BAC) have been consistently closing bank branches for the past couple of years, and will continue to do so throughout 2018 and 2019. One force behind this change are millennial bankers speaking up and saying that “92% of them would choose a bank for its digital services.”
(Source: Mitek Q4 2017 Investor Presentation)
The primary way that Mitek is monetizing this transition is via its Mobile Deposit product. Research firm Futurion released its annual mobile deposit benchmark report which found:
Adoption is growing at a colossal pace. Over 40% of current mobile deposit users adopted the service in the past 12 months. This move is increasingly shifting customers out of the branch and into the mobile channel.
However, Mitek is also well positioned to capture other growth drivers within mobile banking with its Mobile Verify and Mobile Fill products which can be used during bank on-boarding, opening a saving or checking account or applying for a loan. The company predicts that the “number of consumer loans fully approved in the digital channel will double in 2018.”
Another obvious driver in this category is general smartphone user growth. Globally there are currently around 2.3 billion smartphone users which is expected to reach 3 billion in the early 2020s.
(Source: eMarketer study on Statistica)
An increase in the underlying smartphone user base will propagate growth across all of Mitek’s product lines. As more and more consumers have smartphone and camera technology at their fingertips, we will see more and more businesses shift towards mobile-centric business strategies. In fact, “digital media usage has grown 40% since 2013, largely fueled by increased smartphone usage.” This will help enterprises capture additional users while also reducing overhead and processing costs.
A third trend I wanted to speak to in this category is the relatively new blockchain and cryptocurrency trend. I think we will see Mitek come out as a big supporter of this technology given its digital and mobile nature. They believe that by the end of 2018 “50% of international banks will partner with blockchain companies.” Two other names that have been in the news for the past few weeks are Eastman Kodak Company (KODK) and Long Blockchain Corp (LBCC). Both companies announced some sort of blockchain or cryptocurrency integration which was shortly followed by a 200-300% spike in share price.

In fact, Mitek did sell its Mobile Verify product to European blockchain provider Nocks which improved its “customer on-boarding time by 98%, from 12 hours to five minutes. This has helped Nocks grow its user base by 214%.” See the following quick description of Nocks:
Nocks is the first all-digital payments platform built upon the Gulden blockchain – a safe and fast decentralized blockchain that is easy to use for sending or receiving payments with as little effort or cost as possible. Nocks allows consumers and business to pay and get paid using fiat currencies but with the transaction being orchestrated by the Gulden blockchain to improve the speed, transparency and security of payments. Nocks makes paying bills easier, streamlines POS-tools for companies, and offers innovative financial trading mechanisms.
Blockchain has been a real buzzword in the news for the past few months ever since the meteoric rise of Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies throughout Fall and Winter 2017. If we do see a shift towards blockchain-based transactions and payments, Mitek could be uniquely positioned to profit.
Online Security – Data Breaches and Regulations
The other secular trend that I’d like to speak to is an overarching emphasis on improving online security and processes due to past data breaches and new regulations.
The most recent and obvious data breach example was the Equifax (EFX) hack which occurred over summer 2017 and may have impacted as many as 143 million Americans. Mitek discussed this breach during their last earnings call and described it as a direct driver to business. For instance, it was mentioned on the call that a large brokerage firm (name was not disclosed) came to Mitek to implement their Mobile Verify product as a result of the Equifax breach. Another example of a huge breach of information occurred in 2013 when Target (TGT) was hacked and compromised more than 41 million customers’ payment card accounts.
(Source: Aite Group Digital Identification Verification Whitepaper)
Last year, there were more than 80 million fraud attempts at financial institutions using fake or stolen identity credentials. Mitek expects this figure to reach 150 million fraud attempts in 2018, largely due to the Equifax data breach. This could equate to billions of dollars in fraud losses related to applications alone. Mitek is positioned to sell solutions to this exact issue.
New regulatory actions are also pushing firms to step up their security. For instance, the Anti-Money Laundering rules imposed by the Bank Secrecy Act helps “detect and report suspicious activity including the predicate offenses to money laundering and terrorist financing, such as securities fraud and market manipulation.”
In 2015, there were over $5 billion in fines imposed on US banks for violating anti-money laundering regulations. With growing fraudulent activity, and correlated tightening regulations, this figure will only go up which will cause institutions to implement improved security measures.
Another regulatory trend I think we will see regards eCommerce and Sharing Services. Specifically, buyers and sellers being required to verify their identities before doing business. For instance, “Airbnb users can earn a “Verified ID” badge on their profile by providing their online identity (via existing Airbnb reviews, LinkedIn, or Facebook) and matching it to hard copy government issued ID documentation, such as confirming personal information or scanning a photo ID. The name provided by both channels must match for verification to succeed.”
I think we may see similar initiatives across a spectrum of online markets and companies such as Shopify (SHOP), Square (SQ) and eBay (EBAY). Mitek is positioned to provide fast and affordable solutions to these problems by offering digital identity verification in just minutes.
Acquisition Potential
I never think it’s a good idea to base an investment on the possibility of an acquisition or buyout. You should invest in the underlying company, product and/or technology and let the cards fall where they may. However, it’s always a good idea to stay informed.
If you look at the management team at Mitek, you’ll see that it’s filled with folks that built out small tech companies which ended up getting acquired. For instance, CFO Jeff Davison was an executive at two separate tech companies, both of which were bought by Oracle (ORCL). Similarly, CTO Stephen Ritter led the tech team at Emotient, a deep learning facial analytics startup that was bought by Apple (AAPL).
The general idea here is that the team leading Mitek has experience building companies and products that get acquired. Frankly, the products Mitek sells seem like strong acquisition targets to me – they are a cloud-based software company with products and tech that has nearly limitless applications and is relatively easy to implement.
Top Risk Factors
In my research, I came across a handful of risk factors which could impact Mitek’s success. I will summarize the top two which I see to be the most material.
Product competition
Product competition is the risk factor that worries me the most. Not only does Mitek have to worry about its software competitors releasing products that are cheaper and/or more efficient, but they also must worry about their customers developing their own solutions. For instance, Jim DeBello mentioned Apple in a comment during their last earnings call when he referenced the 3D facial recognition technology Apple was working on. It worries me that other tech companies, perhaps with larger R&D coffers, will be able to put a better product on the market.
Litigation regarding intellectual property
Intellectual property concerns also tend to be troublesome for these types of software companies who develop products with massive industry reach. In terms of current legal activity, the firm seems to be clean with the most recent open case closing in July 2016 when the Patent Trial and Appeal Board decided that a patent infringement lawsuit from Rothschild Mobile Imaging Innovations, Inc. was directed towards unpatentable subject matter and thus not eligible.
Mitek also mentions in their 10-K that they are subject to various ongoing claims and legal proceedings which are part of the normal course of their business. They do not believe that these will have any material impact on the firm. Obviously, the big risk factor here is that they are wrong and one of these lawsuits will blow up. Volte-Face Investments, another Seeking Alpha Contributor, put out an interesting article in early 2017 where he draws attention to a potential conflict with USAA where they may request royalties or licensing fees for use of Mobile Deposit platforms to which they contributed initial development work.
There does not seem to be much more information regarding this case, but it will certainly be something to keep an eye open for.
DCF Model and Valuation
I based my model on five years of historical financials (FY13-FY17) and forecasted out ten years at which point I employed a terminal valuation at steady-state growth.
Assumptions
I used three main drivers for my forecast: revenue, SG&A expense and R&D expense. I used these because they play the largest role on Mitek’s bottom line. I rolled out acquisition related expenses across the forecast in anticipation for future M&A activity. I used Mitek’s FY18 guidance of 26-30% revenue growth and 19-20% margins as the foundation for my base case analysis. Bull and bear cases were adjusted from that starting point.
Base Case
My base case valuation used FY18 guidance as a starting point regarding revenue and margins. I slowly improved SG&A expenses relative to revenues to capture improved sales efficiency and additional channels turning online which will make the sales team more impactful. Revenue growth stayed just under 30% and began to shrink over the following years as Mitek’s product lines reach stable-state. R&D expenses remained consistent indicating a steady level of technology reinvestment based on sales.
(Source: self-made forecast using Excel and Mitek financials)
Based on these assumptions, the model returned a range of share prices in a Cost of Equity vs. Terminal Growth sensitivity analysis. I see fair value falling between $9.78 and $14.14 per share. This indicates an average of 25% upside to current price.
Bull Case
My bull case valuation assumes FY18 guidance is conservative and that we will see better growth and improving margins on sales and operations. SG&A costs relative to revenues improved more rapidly as new channels turn online and less relative sales and marketing activities are required. Revenue growth was pegged at 40% for 2018 and began to decrease from there as Mitek’s product lines reach stable-state. R&D expenses increased moderately which indicates increases in technological development to better provide for the growing and adapting consumer pipeline.
(Source: self-made forecast using Excel and Mitek financials)
Assuming higher than forecasted revenue growth with improving operating margins, the same model returned a range of $13.63-$19.82 in my high probability region which indicates an average of 75% upside to share price.
Bear Case
My bear case analysis assumes that FY18 guidance is too aggressive and/or there will be issues in the underlying technology and product portfolio. This could indicate that a competitor introduces better tech into this marketplace, for example. FY18 revenues grow under 20% and are reduced to single-digit steady state quickly. SG&A expenses creep up slowly which implies poor efficiency in converting marketing and sales work to new customers and revenue. R&D expenses stay mostly stable.
(Source: self-made forecast using Excel and Mitek financials)
Assuming decreasing revenues and poor operating efficiency returns a share range of $3.34-$4.63 in my high probability range. This indicates a 57% downside to current share prices
Conclusion
Concluding my thoughts, I see Mitek as a solid growth play across many changing and adapting mobile/digital driven markets. They have a technologically concise product portfolio which provides solutions across multiple different secular trends. I see substantial upside in my base and bull cases with similar downside if problems arise. The key thing to keep an eye on will be competitors putting out technologies that are superior and/or at a cheaper price.
Assuming that Mitek can remain on the forefront of digital and mobile identity verification and mobile banking, I think they will be a strong small-cap play that could pay off big time. Additionally, I expect a very strong earnings call later this week due to a few event-driven catalysts.
